title: Sidama Chuko
author: Mama Tigist

heritage.origin: Sidama people — Sidama region around Lake Hawassa
heritage.history: The Sidama are one of the largest non-Semitic ethnic groups in Ethiopia, living around Lake Hawassa in the Rift Valley. Their cuisine centres on enset (like the Gurage) but also uses sorghum and maize. Chuko is the fermented enset preparation specific to the Sidama — slightly different from Gurage Kocho in its processing method and flavour. The Sidama also grow some of Ethiopia's finest coffee in the Sidama Zone, and their food culture reflects their position between the enset-eating southern highlands and the coffee-growing traditions.

desc: Sidama Chuko — Sidama-style fermented enset bread with spiced lamb or vegetable sauce. The central staple of Sidama cuisine — different from Gurage Kocho in its shorter fermentation and moister texture.
longDesc: Chuko represents the Sidama enset tradition — the false banana plant that feeds the Sidama people. The Sidama preparation ferments the enset starch for a shorter period than the Gurage method, producing a moister, more pliable result.
ingredients: // Chuko base: substitute with Kocho (ETH003) if enset not available
steps: Cook Sidama lamb sauce: sauté onions. Add garlic and spices.
Add lamb. Brown. Add tomatoes. Simmer 45 minutes.
Serve lamb sauce alongside Chuko with fresh collard greens.
chefTips: Sidama lamb sauce uses less spice than Amhara wat — more subtle.
commonMistakes: Over-spicing — Sidama food is milder than Amhara.
cookingScience: See ETH003 for enset fermentation science.
sustainabilityTips: Enset — one of the world's most sustainable food plants.
culturalNote: Sidama Chuko is the food that sustained the Sidama people through centuries of history in the Rift Valley — the enset plant that grows where other food plants cannot, and the simple lamb sauce that reflects the pastoral traditions of the region.
